from.place: the canonical structural map in the strict henselization limit used in the proof of Tag 03Q9

title: Structural map of the strict henselization
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and let $S_{(\bar s)}=\lim_{(V,\bar v)}V$ be the strict henselization, with limit projections $\pi_V:S_{(\bar s)}\to V$ over the affine pointed etale neighbourhoods $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar s$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. The *structural morphism* $\rho_{\bar s}:S_{(\bar s)}\to S$ is the composite of $\pi_V$ with the structure morphism $V\to S$, for any $(V,\bar v)$. It does not depend on $(V,\bar v)$: the projections are compatible with the pointed morphisms of neighbourhoods, which are morphisms over $S$, and the category of affine pointed neighbourhoods is cofiltered, hence nonempty and connected [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit].

source.place: Theorem Tag 03Q9 proof, strict henselization inverse limit structural map

proof.text: Apply strictHenselization_properties to obtain cofilteredness of the small representative category. For an arrow i to j, cone naturality identifies the j leg with the i leg followed by Spec of the global-sections map. Apply Spec.map to ΓSpecIso_inv_naturality for the underlying ring map. Associativity and the affine-neighbourhood morphism condition over S show that the composites to S agree.

Choose one representative j0 using nonemptiness. For any j, IsCofiltered.min j j0 has arrows to both j and j0. The arrowwise equalities from the preceding step identify the composite for j with the composite for j0. Choose the latter as rho.

Reuse the proved upstream existence theorem and structural map with their identical signatures. Consumers obtain the representative leg equation directly from Classical.choose_spec of exists_strictHenselizationStructuralMap. The redundant Sheaf compatibility wrapper is retired; no identification with strictLocalization is required.
